verdict.rationale: Aider documents its own programmatic interfaces: a `--message` CLI mode that applies one instruction and exits, and a Python scripting API (`Coder.create` / `coder.run`). Most options can also be set by switch, config file or environment variable. Nothing shows these interfaces reach parity with the interactive chat (/add, /undo, /architect, /voice, /web, the browser UI), and probes found no OpenAPI or HTTP API surface. missing for 10: documented parity of the scripting API with all in-chat commands and modes, a formal API reference or HTTP API spec, independent corroboration of full programmatic coverage.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can do everything through the API that I can do in the UI

citations.quote: Aider takes a `--message` argument, where you can give it a natural language instruction. It will do that one thing, apply the edits to the files and then exit.
Aider has many options which can be set with command line switches. Most options can also be set in an `.aider.conf.yml` file... Or by setting environment variables like `AIDER_xxx`
